title: Sample Surgery: DevExp sync — QA / quickstart handoff
agenda:
1) Quickstart QA handoff status
2) Samples repo triage: flaky templates + CI failures
3) SDK example surface: sync with v0.9 changes
4) Doc playbook: onboarding concision pass
5) Action items and owners
notes:
Summary: Short, tactical sync to prepare the quickstart package for the incoming QA cycle and freeze the sample template API for the SDK v0.9 rollout. Meeting focused on removing a few flaky test harnesses, aligning telemetry/event names, and deciding the minimal README layout for user onboarding.

Highlights:
- QA handoff: Lina ran smoke on 6 core quickstarts; 4 passed, 2 failed intermittently (auth and streaming examples). Flaky failures tied to CI environment (docker networking timeouts) and a recent change in the SDK streaming callback semantics.
- Samples repo triage: Ben identified 3 template variants that diverged from the canonical example; we agreed to consolidate into a single template plus 2 specialized variants (auth, file-upload).
- SDK v0.9 changes: Samir walked through the breaking rename of `stream_handler` -> `on_stream_chunk` and the new auth token refresh helpers. We flagged all examples that call `stream_handler` as needing patch PRs.
- Docs playbook: Marcus proposed a 2-column README pattern (left: minimal quickstart copy, right: common troubleshooting bullets). Consensus was to adopt for all quickstarts to reduce first-run friction.
- Telemetry: Arielle suggested standard event names: `quickstart.start`, `quickstart.complete`, `quickstart.error`, and `quickstart.env` attribute for mode (hosted|dedicated|private). Lina asked that events include a sample_id to map failures to examples.

Notes-to-self / informal bits:
- We are okay shipping with 2 known flaky CI tests if they are annotated and excluded from gating (non-blocking).
- Keep the migration PRs to SDK examples small (one example per PR) to make QA easier.
- Add a tiny checklist at top of each sample README: prerequisites, run command, expected output (one-liner), common error codes.

Decisions (short):
- Freeze sample template API for v0.9 today (no new template fields until post-release).
- Consolidate templates: canonical + auth + file-upload variants.
- Telemetry event names standardized (see linked list) and sample_id required.
- Flaky CI tests will be marked as ``non-gating`` for the QA handoff; a follow-up infra ticket created to investigate.

Blockers:
- CI docker networking instability (infra ticket ENG-3742) — blocks full green runs for samples.
- Token refresh bug in SDK helper (PR link in artifacts) — blocks streaming auth example.

Context / background: The quickstarts are the primary onboarding surface for new users hitting the hosted API and also used in partner onboarding. We want the first-run to be predictable: single command, <30s runtime, deterministic stdout, and clear remediation steps. This meeting was intended to create a minimal, testable contract for that flow so QA can sign off quickly.
decisions: Freeze sample template API for SDK v0.9
Consolidate templates into canonical + auth + file-upload
Standardize telemetry event names and require sample_id
Mark flaky CI checks as non-gating for the handoff

references:
Quickstart checklist template (draft):
- prerequisites: python 3.10, pip, REDWOOD_API_KEY env var
- install: pip install redwood-sdk
- run: python quickstart.py --example minimal
- expected: prints a 1-line json with `choice` key and exits
- troubleshooting: token 401 -> confirm env var, network timeout -> retry with --no-stream
